title: 📋 Academic vs General Training — What's the Difference?

sections.heading: Two versions of IELTS
sections.body:
IELTS has two versions:

🎓 ACADEMIC — for undergraduate/postgraduate study or professional registration
📋 GENERAL TRAINING — for secondary education, work experience, or immigration

Listening and Speaking: IDENTICAL in both versions
Reading and Writing Task 1: DIFFERENT between versions

sections.heading: Reading differences
sections.body:
ACADEMIC Reading:
• 3 long, complex passages from books, journals, magazines
• Dense academic vocabulary and argument structure
• Topics: science, technology, environment, social issues

GENERAL TRAINING Reading:
• Section A: everyday notices, advertisements, timetables
• Section B: workplace documents, policies, guidelines
• Section C: one longer text similar to Academic

highlight: Using the WRONG version will invalidate your result. Always confirm which version your institution or visa requires BEFORE booking your test.

title: ✍️ Writing Task 1 — The Key Difference
body:
ACADEMIC Writing Task 1:
Describe a graph, chart, diagram, or map
'Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features'
Requires: overview + data description + comparisons

GENERAL TRAINING Writing Task 1:
Write a letter (formal, semi-formal, or informal)
'Write a letter to... explaining / requesting / complaining about...'
Requires: appropriate register + clear purpose + all bullet points covered

Writing Task 2 is IDENTICAL: a discursive essay on a general topic.

quick.label: Task 2 essay: same for both versions

question: You are applying for a master's degree at a UK university. Which IELTS version should you take?
options: IELTS for UKVI — always required for the UK
explanation:
Universities require ACADEMIC IELTS for undergraduate and postgraduate admission.

General Training is designed for:
• Skilled migration visas
• Work experience programs
• Secondary school enrollment
• Some professional registration pathways

Note: IELTS for UKVI is a variant required specifically for UK visa applications — but the academic/general distinction still applies within UKVI versions.

question: In IELTS Academic, Writing Task 1 asks you to:
options: Write a formal letter to a company
Describe a graph, chart, map, or process diagram
Write a personal essay about your life
correct: Describe a graph, chart, map, or process diagram
explanation:
Academic Task 1 (150+ words, 20 minutes):
✅ Graphs (line, bar, pie)
✅ Tables
✅ Maps (before/after)
✅ Process/flow diagrams

You summarise and compare the key features without giving personal opinions.

General Training Task 1 is a letter — completely different!
hint: Academic Task 1 is always visual data — never a letter.

question: Which parts of IELTS are IDENTICAL in both Academic and General Training?
explanation:
✅ SAME: Listening + Speaking
❌ DIFFERENT: Reading (text types differ) + Writing Task 1 (graph vs letter)

Writing Task 2 is essentially the same in both — a discursive essay, though General Training essays are generally considered slightly easier in practice.
hint: Only two sections are different — which two have different text types or task types?

title: Academic vs General Training — Spot the Error
instruction: Which statement about IELTS versions is INCORRECT?

sentences.text: Academic IELTS is required for university admission in most countries.
The Speaking test is different in Academic and General Training IELTS.
sentences.explanation:
The Speaking test is IDENTICAL in both versions — same format, same criteria, same examiner approach.

Only Reading and Writing Task 1 differ between Academic and General Training.

sentences.text: General Training Writing Task 1 requires writing a letter rather than describing data.
